fda_source_note: FDA NDA/priority-review cycle verified for chronic hepatitis B with PDUFA 2026-10-26; Breakthrough and Fast Track designations reported. B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials met the primary endpoint; pooled functional cure 19% (233/1220) vs 0/614, p<0.001 in both trials; 26% vs 0% in lower-HBsAg subgroup. Safety was acceptable but not trivial: pooled on-treatment AEs 89% vs 65% placebo, serious AEs 4% vs 1%, treatment-related serious AEs 2%; discontinuation about 3%. As of 2026-10-06 no earlier U.S. FDA final action was identified. Sources: https://www.gsk.com/en-gb/media/press-releases/bepirovirsen-achieves-unprecedented-functional-cure-rates-with-potential-to-redefine-treatment-for-chronic-hepatitis-b/ ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1131399/000165495426003977/a1144c.htm

fda_source_note: BLA accepted for accelerated-approval review, PDUFA 2026-10-30; FDA denied requested Priority Review and initially questioned whether accelerated-approval eligibility was adequately justified. RRP-001 was Phase 1/2, single-arm, n=32: 81.3% reduced surgeries, 28.1% required no surgery during the following year; median decrease 3 surgeries with 95% CI 2-3; all treatment-related AEs were grade 1-2, no treatment-related SAEs. By August 2026 INOVIO reported late-cycle review completed and all scheduled pre-licensure inspections completed; FDA did not discuss the earlier accelerated-approval concern at an informal clinical meeting, but no public final inspection/CMC outcome was disclosed. As of 2026-10-06 no earlier FDA final action was identified. fda_source_note: sNDA for accelerated approval in sickle cell disease accepted with Priority Review; PDUFA 2026-11-01; confirmatory REIGNITE Phase 3 initiated. RISE UP Phase 3 randomized 207 patients. Hemoglobin-response primary endpoint strongly positive: 40.6% vs 2.9%, p<0.0001. Hemoglobin and indirect-bilirubin key secondary endpoints also p<0.0001. However, the annualized sickle-cell pain-crisis co-primary endpoint did not reach significance (2.62 vs 3.05; p=0.1213), and PROMIS Fatigue key secondary endpoint was not met (p=0.7112). Safety was reported consistent with prior mitapivat experience. As of 2026-10-06 no earlier FDA final action was identified.
